english_translation: Dense green bushland grows with various plant species and thorny thistles that have not yet dried out.

dialogue.shona: Bundo rakawanda rakasvibira riine marudzi akasiyana nezvidhongi zvinobaya zvisati zvaoma.
dialogue.english: Dense green bushland grows with various plant species and thorny thistles that have not yet dried out.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Bundo [bundo] • rakawanda [it (past) wanda] • rakasvibira [it (past) svibira] • riine [riine] • marudzi [plural rudzi] • akasiyana [he/she (past) siyana] • nezvidhongi [and / with zvidhongi] • zvinobaya [things nobaya]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('rakawanda')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'rakawanda' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('zvinobaya')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'zvinobaya' uses the present marker '-no-'. In Shona, inserting '-no-' between the subject prefix and the verb stem expresses general truths, everyday habits, or states of mind like 'wanting', 'thinking', and 'knowing'. For example: 'ndinoda' ('I want/like'), 'unofunga' ('you think'), 'vanoti' ('they say'), and 'vanorima' ('they farm').
grammar_notes.rule: [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

grammar_notes.title: Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nezvidhongi'
grammar_notes.content: Look closely at 'nezvidhongi'. In Shona, the word for 'and' or 'with' between nouns is not a separate word—instead, the prefix 'ne-' (or 'na-' before people's names) is written attached directly to the second noun! For example, 'ne-' + 'zvidhongi' forms 'nezvidhongi'. You will see this everywhere in daily speech: 'sadza nemuriwo' ('sadza and vegetables'), 'nesimba' ('with strength'), and 'nekukasira' ('with haste / quickly').
grammar_notes.rule: ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

cultural_notes.title: Savanna Bushland ('Bundo') & Thorny Flora After the Rains
cultural_notes.content: During the rainy season ('zhizha'), Zimbabwe's highveld and lowveld burst into thick green bushland ('bundo rakasvibira') dotted with hardy thorny plants ('zvidhongi zvinobaya') that stay green well into the beginning of the dry season.
